open_errors.issue: Rohan has hunted for an ear-wound since ch 2. In ch 18 Kiran's frostbitten ear 'stood out' while Rohan stood in the doorway. Ch 21 then hides both ears under a wool cap, and ch 22 treats the passage as Rohan's first look at the torn rim. As written, the hunter sees the very clue he asked the village about and ignores it for four chapters.
open_errors.fix: Cover the ear with the wool cap from Kiran's first appearance, matching ch 21 and ch 22.

patches.find: The frostbitten ear, curled and puckered like a dried apricot, stood out against a face that had lost its flesh.
patches.replace: A wool cap was pulled down over both ears, hiding the frostbitten one, and under it his face had lost its flesh.

open_errors.issue: The bible says the red rope was spun in Lata's house. Ch 1 says Bindu got the raw wool from Lata, which means Bindu spun it. The same sentence also says the wool was 'begged' and then 'sold'.
open_errors.fix: Say the wool was spun in Lata's house and sold to the crew.

patches.find: Bindu had begged the raw wool off a Taravan trader, Lata, who sold to them at a fair price and asked nothing.
patches.replace: The wool had been spun in the house of a Taravan trader, Lata, who sold to them at a fair price and asked nothing.

open_errors.issue: In ch 2 Rohan draws the writ from his coat. In ch 7 it lives in a stamped writ case on his belt, and he only moves it into his coat after Meera cuts the case for goggles.
open_errors.fix: Have him draw the writ from the case at his belt in ch 2.

patches.find: Rohan drew the writ from his coat and unfolded it so the back rows could see the brown ink and the crown's red border.
patches.replace: Rohan drew the writ from the leather case at his belt and unfolded it so the back rows could see the brown ink and the crown's red border.

open_errors.issue: Meera recalls counting the gully party 'on the rope'. Nobody was roped in the gully. They crossed the bowl one at a time, thirty paces apart, and were only bound later at the cairn.

patches.find: She had counted them on the rope herself.
patches.replace: She had counted them on the slope herself.

open_errors.issue: Meera asks 'What?' and Rohan answers 'Nothing.' when something plainly is wrong. That is a false statement made to be believed, yet his hands stay warm, and the bible never waives the cost. The narration's 'refusal' reading needs a reply that is actually a refusal.
open_errors.fix: Make the reply a deferral that is true.

open_errors.issue: Redbark is rust-red or blood-coloured everywhere else (ch 2, 4, 11), and this twist is said to match Meera's crown-grade stock. In ch 15 it is described as 'pale brown'.

patches.find: Powder, pale brown, and a smell like old tea and bitter bark.
patches.replace: Powder, rust-red, and a smell like old tea and bitter bark.

open_errors.issue: Soldiers 'ran their hands down every seam' of Rohan's coat and found only the speech, his knife and Dilan's rope end. Yet the writ is still in his coat in ch 30 and 31, and in ch 30 he draws from it the flat tin holding the queen's wax and her signed line.
open_errors.fix: Have the search find the writ and the tin, with Varun dismissing them as worthless without the stone.

patches.find: They found the speech on the back of Nimmi's tally sheet. Varun read it, smiled, and slid it back into the lining.
patches.replace: They found the speech on the back of Nimmi's tally sheet, the folded writ and a flat tin of wax. Varun read the speech, smiled, glanced at the rest as a man glances at a lock without its key, and slid it all back into the lining.

open_errors.issue: In ch 1 the brass button token was stitched into the ledger's spine 'where only a person who unpicked the binding would find it'. In ch 28 it simply comes out when Meera reaches in with two fingers.
open_errors.fix: Have her pick the stitches to free it.

patches.find: She reached into the binding of the count with two fingers, and the little thing came out onto her palm.
patches.replace: She picked the stitches in the binding of the count with her thumbnail, and the little thing came out onto her palm.

open_errors.issue: Asha freed Rohan before dawn on the day before the Fair, and the party then walked a full day and a night to reach the meadow. Varun calls the escape 'last night'.

patches.find: He broke custody at Ranu last night with a smuggler's help.
patches.replace: He broke custody at Ranu yesterday with a smuggler's help.
